metadata.title: Forming Young and Hypervelocity Stars in the Galactic Centre via Tidal Disruption of a Molecular Cloud

evidence.quote: Koposov et al. (2020) discovered a hypervelocity star (S5-HVS1) that was ejected from the Galactic centre (GC) 4.8 Myr ago.
The recent discovery of a hypervelocity star S5-HVS1
Koposov et al. (2020) discovered a hypervelocity star (S5-HVS1) that was ejected from the Galactic centre (GC) 4.8 Myr ago.
Recently Koposov et al. (2020) discovered a hypervelocity star that was ejected from the Galactic centre 5 Myr ago.
In fact, S5-HVS1 could be such a star

notes: S5-HVS1: previously discovered as a hypervelocity star ejected from the Galactic centre (T:p1-b10), and this paper uses it as an observational constraint and discusses its possible origin (T:p14-b10, T:p14-b12). The paper does not explicitly say Galactic unbound; inclusion follows the field-standard interpretation of a hypervelocity star as a Galactic unbound candidate. No other individual stars are identified; S-stars, clockwise-disc stars, and simulated ejected particles are populations without individual identifiers.

S5-HVS1: S5-HVS1 is only mentioned in the context of its discovery and origin. The paper reports an ejection time of 4.8 Myr ago (also described as ~5 Myr), a velocity vector consistent with a disk origin (~10% probability of random alignment given the ~7 deg disc half-opening angle), and a spectroscopic age of 25-93 Myr (Koposov et al. 2020) at T:p1-b10 and T:p1-b12. None of these are values of the requested quantities (ra, dec, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability); no numerical position or kinematic values for S5-HVS1 are given. The ejection/age values are therefore not recorded.
